#### List:

- Key numbers
- Carriage
- Variable CO~2~ affinity

#### Carriage:

+-----------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| As HCO~3~^-^          | - Location:                                                                                                                                                        |
|                       |   - Haemoglobin (140g/L, 39 imidazoles per molecule)                                                                                                               |
|                       |   - Plasma proteins (70g/L, 13 imidazoles per molecule)                                                                                                            |
|                       | - Purpose:                                                                                                                                                         |
|                       |   - Maintain partial pressure gradient for CO~2~ from tissues into capillary blood                                                                                 |
|                       | - Mechanism:                                                                                                                                                       |
|                       |   - CO~2~ + H~2~O \< -\> H^+^ + HCO~3~^-^ (catalysed by carbonic anhydrase in RBC)                                                                                 |
|                       |   - KHb + H^+^ \<-\> HHb + K^+^ (buffering by imidazole groups of histidine residues)                                                                              |
|                       |   - HCO~3~^-^ exchanged for Cl^-^ at membrane (Hamburger effect, facilitates above reactions)                                                                      |
+-----------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| As carbamino compound | - Location: same                                                                                                                                                   |
|                       | - Purpose: same                                                                                                                                                    |
|                       | - Mechanism: NH~2~ + CO~2~ \<-\> NHCOO^-^ + H^+^                                                                                                                   |
+-----------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| As dissolved          | - Amount dissolved = PaCO~2~ x k (Henry’s law)                                                                                                                     |
|                       | - Solubility coefficient k: 0.03mmol/L/mmHg at 37°C                                                                                                                |
|                       | - Note ↑temp → ↓solubility → ↑PaCO~2~:CaCO~2~                                                                                                                      |
+-----------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Illustration          | ![](/content/exams/anzca/2019/A/4/prize-image001.jpg){fig-alt="Carbon dioxide reactions in erythrocytes, haemoglobin buffering and chloride–bicarbonate exchange"} |
+-----------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

#### Variable CO~2~ affinity:

+---------------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Haldane effect      | - Higher uptake of CO~2~ and H^+^ in HHb c.f. HbO~2~:                            |
|                     |   - 70% of increment due to 3.5x ↑carbamino formation                            |
|                     |   - 30% of increment due to ↑buffering (imidazole pKa 6.6 → 8.2)                 |
+---------------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Isohydric buffering | - For each mol O~2~ unloaded by Hb, 0.7mol H^+^ can be added without ↓ plasma pH |
|                     | - Due to Haldane effect                                                          |
+---------------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
